_method_note: Structured cross-references between locations, time periods, characters, and concepts found across the material set. Every entry lists its source file(s). Nothing here is asserted beyond what a source states; where sources disagree, both values are kept and a matching entry is added to 'conflicts'. Full prose per source lives in material/_context.md; this file is the associative index. Sources are abbreviated: atlax_i, atlax_ii, catastro, ensayo_i, libro, timelines_py (timelines.py), esquema (ESQUEMA.pdf), book_of_inventions, cartography_highways/cartography_trains/cartography_airports (Cartography (Map Markers) [Code].xlsx), luminacion_register (Luminacion Register [Code].xlsx), mapa_del_milenio (El Antiguo Continente de Milkan - Mapa del Milenio.png), plus 5 dated/named screenshots (Khan Ice WP, Sid Nalta WP, Milka General Map, Milka Oceans Plan and Continent Outline, Ruta Lundria-Salthos Cruzados) referenced inline by filename. Per the user (2026-07-24), 'Luminacion Register' and 'Terraforming Regions Purge Register.xlsx' ARE lore sources, split into a narrative layer (named characters/locations/actions - captured under characters.named_inhabitants) and a technical/'mysterious formula' layer (Clock-worldTime triggers, Taterzen movement logic, region-purge flags - left undeciphered, see unknowns.md) - not excluded, just not yet interpreted. Some conflict entries also carry a 'user_resolution' field: a design decision the user gave directly (not derived from any document), dated. These sit alongside the documentary facts rather than replacing them. IMPORTANT: everything above this line, and everything in 'locations'/'time_systems'/'routes'/'characters'/'concepts'/'conflicts' below, is the OBJECTIVE record - reconstructed from primary materials, per the archaeologist method. A second, SUBJECTIVE record sits alongside it: the top-level 'hearsay' array near the end of this file, mirroring _lore/hearsay/hearsay.md, logging what characters have actually said in played Blabber dialogues - never merged into the objective arrays above and never treated as corroborating them, even when they happen to agree; see 'hearsay._method_note' for the exact shape, including how a claim's consistency with the record and with facts is tracked. A third, OBJECTIVE-track array (not subjective like 'hearsay') is 'tales', fed by the /tell skill and mirrored in _lore/tales/: told/stated directly by the user, the world's author, folded into locations/characters/concepts/routes/time_systems via a 'tale:<id>' source tag, and into 'conflicts' on disagreement, by the same rules as any material source; see that array's own _method_note for the exact shape, including 'told_by' vs 'responsible'. Update (2026-07-26): 'ensayo_i_final' is a later, July 2026 edition of ensayo_i ('ENSAYO I (Final Version).pdf'), by the same credited author under an expanded byline ('Iläria Astraëa desde la lejana ciudad de Lündria'). Where the two editions disagree, both are kept, per the same disagreement rule as every other source pair - see CONFLICT-15, CONFLICT-16, CONFLICT-17.
_categories_method_note: Describes how scripts/lore/sample_lore_knowledge.py flattens each category below into sample-able pool items, so the set of categories is read from this data rather than hardcoded per-path loops in the script. 'shape' selects a handler: 'list' (a flat list of dicts at 'path', identified by 'id_field', pool text built by joining 'text_fields') covers most categories and is the default shape for any new category with that structure; 'grouped_list' and 'claims' are special-cased for characters.named_inhabitants.by_locality and hearsay.entries respectively, since neither is a flat list. When /integrate approves a genuinely new category, it adds an entry here (and, if the shape isn't 'list', a new handler in SHAPE_HANDLERS) - no epistemology metadata needs authoring per category anymore (see next). 'has_sources' (bool) marks whether entries in this category carry a 'sources' list (provenance, see .claude/skills/integrate/SKILL.md Pass 1 step 3) - scripts/lore/build_source_index.py reads this to know which categories it should link hearsay/tale references into, instead of a hardcoded category list. Removed 2026-08-16: a per-category 'epistemology_group' field used to drive /character Step 4d's trusts/distrusts derivation. Replaced with per-ITEM provenance derivation (material/hearsay/tale, read from an anchor's own 'sources[0].category', or trivially 'hearsay'/'tale' when the anchor's own category already IS one of those, with 'conflict' kept as a fixed special case outside this system entirely) - see scripts/lore/anchor_epistemology.py and /character Step 4d for the current mechanism. A category-level classification never made sense here: two items in the same category (e.g. two locations) can have completely different provenance, which epistemology_group could never express.

routes._method_note: From cartography (Cartography (Map Markers) [Code].xlsx). Individual waypoints are not reproduced here (hundreds per route) - only named endpoints/waypoints and total distances. All coordinates are X,Z pairs unless noted.

hearsay._method_note: SUBJECTIVE record, distinct from every array above. Mirrors _lore/characters/hearsay.md exactly - one entry per real (non-template) dialog file in data/luminacion/blabber/dialogues/. 'claims' are what a character asserted, not verified facts; 'about' cross-references an id in 'locations'/'concepts'/'conflicts' above ONLY to mark topical overlap, never as corroboration. Consistency is recorded INCONSISTENT-ONLY: a field is present on a claim only when a genuine contradiction was actually found; absence means either 'checked and matches' or 'nothing to check against yet' - recording the unremarkable case explicitly on every claim would just be noise. Two independent flags: (1) 'inconsistent_with_record', an array of {about, source_kind, note} objects - present only when the claim contradicts something in the objective arrays above ('about' names the contradicted entry/CONFLICT id, 'source_kind' is 'material'/'tale' naming which of the two kinds of objective source the contradicted entry rests on, since disbelieving a written map and disbelieving something someone was told directly are different in kind - a character might reasonably distrust one and not the other; 'note' explains the contradiction in one sentence). (2) 'inconsistent_with_facts', a plain string (present only when true, value = the explanation) - set when a claim contradicts one of the two universal facts in _lore/facts/facts.json. No 'fact_ref' id is needed: there are only two facts, they are baked into every character unconditionally, and checking against them means reading facts.json directly, not looking up an id. A claim can also surface a genuine gap rather than a contradiction - something the objective record has never addressed at all, not something it disagrees with; when that happens and it resonates with the existing corpus, log it in _lore/unknowns.md (cross-referencing the claim's id), matching the file's existing shape, the same way material and tale do. Not every claim produces one - skip rather than manufacturing a question that isn't genuinely there. Since scripts/lore/sample_lore_knowledge.py draws individual claims from this array into a character's knowledge pool at the same odds as any objective-record fact (see README §8 Step 1), a claim can now be retold by a new character and logged again as a fresh claim. Whenever that happens, scripts/lore/lineage_coin.py rolls a flat 50/50 to decide whether the origin survives the retelling: 'traceable' sets 'derived_from' (a claim id, e.g. 'nawom_morkulo_first_meeting#5') and the dialog line may cite the source by name; 'untraceable' leaves 'derived_from' unset and sets 'oral_lore': true instead - no origin recorded, dialog line uses vague framing ('they say...'), regardless of whether the content itself has drifted. 'oral_lore' can also be set true (paired with a 'note' explaining what grew) on a claim that traces back fine but has still accumulated specifics beyond what its 'about' grounding supports. Most claims have none of these fields - they're unremarkable, either freshly sampled from the objective record or a faithful, traceable retelling.

tales._method_note: A THIRD kind of source, distinct from both the objective record above and 'hearsay' - see _lore/tales/_index.md. A tale is told directly by the user, the world's author, outside any character's mouth and outside any excavated document - whether framed as a narrated story or stated plainly as a fact now known. Deliberately not distinguishing those two framings with a fact/fiction label: a tale can be partly true, the way a real legend often is, and that ambiguity is the point. Unlike hearsay, a tale IS folded into the objective arrays above (locations/characters/concepts/routes/time_systems) wherever it overlaps an existing entry - via a 'tale:<id>' item added to that entry's 'sources' list, exactly like a material-file abbreviation - never by overwriting an existing entry. A genuine disagreement with something already on record gets a new 'conflicts' entry (next CONFLICT-NN id), 'user_resolution' left unset. Populated by the /tell skill (.claude/skills/tell/SKILL.md). Each entry here is a manifest of one tale, not a duplicate of its content: 'touches' lists every id (in any array above, including 'conflicts') this tale added or amended - the full text lives in _lore/tales/<id>.md. 'told_by' (nullable) names who is credited IN-FICTION with this tale, if it's framed that way (a character, an institution, a legend) - both a name and 'nobody' are genuine, deliberate answers; most tales leave it null since there's usually no in-world frame at all. Who (which real-world user) actually recorded the entry is a separate question, answered in _lore/tales/_authors.md, never here.
